beats.narration_text: What Claude actually is. You type something, it types back. It can write, think, summarize, analyze documents, work with your files, help you make decisions. It's made by Anthropic. If you've used ChatGPT, Claude is the same species — you interact with both the same way. If you've never used any AI, Claude is a good place to start. Three things will save you from the most common beginner mistakes.

Claude vs. ChatGPT — the comparison everyone asks for. Same species, different personality. Writing voice: Claude's default is less AI-flavored. Long documents: Claude reads a 200-page document in one go without losing track. File work: Claude's desktop app can see your local folder and work with your files directly — ChatGPT can't yet. Multi-step jobs: Claude has Cowork, which runs tasks for 30 minutes and hands you a finished thing. That's the real difference.

How to actually start. Go to claude.ai. Create an account — you need to verify your phone. The free plan gives you Sonnet 4.6. Pay twenty dollars a month for Pro and you get Opus 4.7 — the smartest model. Set thinking to High, turn on Thinking mode. That's the setup. Now the infamous prompt. You don't need to write like an engineer. One technique outperforms every prompt template you've ever saved.

beats.narration_text: The technique is AskUserQuestion. Instead of you writing a perfect prompt, you give Claude a task and tell it to ask you the questions it needs. Claude prompts you. You click answers. The output after three to five questions is better than what you'd get from twenty minutes of prompt engineering. Write it on your hand. 'Help me do X. Use AskUserQuestion first.' That one line puts you ahead of most Claude users.

beats.narration_text: Claude has three modes and they do very different things. Chat is the browser or app — type a question, get an answer, copy the text. Cowork is the desktop app's middle tab — it runs multiple Claudes in parallel, generates actual files saved to your computer, and handles 30-minute tasks. Code is for developers building software. If you don't code, you want Chat and Cowork. Cowork is the one that changes how you work.

First Cowork session. Download the desktop app at claude.ai/download. Open it, click the Cowork tab. Create one clean folder on your computer — call it Cowork. No passwords, nothing you'd hate to lose — Claude can see everything inside it. Select that folder in Cowork. Now drop in a messy document, an old proposal, last month's numbers. Use the AskUserQuestion trick. Three minutes later: a clean Excel file, a real PDF, sitting in your folder.

How the people who use Claude well actually use it. Skills and Connectors. A Skill is a slash command — a capability you call from any chat. Type /skill-name and Claude runs your pre-written instructions without you repeating them. A Connector bridges Claude to an app you already pay for: Gmail, Slack, Notion, Granola, HubSpot. Ask Claude 'what's pending in my Gmail this week?' and it reads your actual inbox. Zero copy-paste. That's the real lever.
Your turn. Ten minutes this week. Open Claude, pick Opus 4.7, turn on Thinking. Paste this prompt. Don't optimize. Don't craft. Just type your actual task and let Claude ask you the questions.
